meta.name: Security Probe Research — Session Router
meta.description: Web research graph for issue #1253 — dual-target security audit

properties.title: Quarkslab Audit of Session (2021)
properties.overall_assessment: Good security level, usable for privacy-concerned people
properties.severe_finding: Android TLS verification bypass when fetching service node list — MITM via malicious CA
properties.note: Audit covered Session app, NOT session-router/lokinet layer

properties.title: Session Protocol V2 — PFS + Post-Quantum
changes: Re-introducing Perfect Forward Secrecy via rotating key pairs
Per-device rotating keys + shared per-account rotating key
Linked device management and remote revocation
properties.security_implication: V2 changes key exchange fundamentally — our session init/accept will need updating

properties.title: QUIC-Fuzz: Effective Greybox Fuzzer for QUIC (ESORICS 2025)
properties.findings: 10 new vulnerabilities, 2 CVE assignments across 6 implementations
properties.technique: Greybox fuzzing, 84% more code coverage than prior fuzzers
properties.targets_tested: Google, Alibaba, and 4 other QUIC server implementations
properties.relevance: Same technique applicable to oxen-libquic

properties.title: QUIC-LEAK CVE-2025-54939 — Pre-handshake DoS in LSQUIC
properties.mechanism: Memory exhaustion before handshake — bypasses all QUIC protections
properties.relevance: Pre-handshake resource exhaustion is directly applicable to our probe design

properties.title: Revisiting QUIC Attacks — Comprehensive Review (Springer 2022)
properties.relevance: Comprehensive taxonomy — every category should map to a probe

properties.title: QUIC Security & Privacy Survey (IEEE 2024)
properties.scope: Comprehensive survey of QUIC vulnerabilities, threats, attacks
properties.key_insight: QUIC's benefits (reduced latency, connection migration, default encryption) introduce new attack surfaces

properties.title: oxen-libquic Stability Crashes (2024)
properties.context: iOS QUIC connections uncovered crash cases in oxen-libquic affecting storage server
properties.impact: Any crash along onion path interrupts ALL connections through that node — cascading failure
properties.fix: Mandatory service node upgrade with oxen-libquic fixes
properties.relevance: Crash-on-unexpected-input is exactly what our probes should find

properties.title: De-anonymisation Attacks on Tor: A Survey
properties.key_stat: 32% of Tor research focuses on deanonymization attacks
properties.session_relevance: Session uses 3-hop onion routing like Tor — same attack classes apply

properties.title: DeTorrent: Adversarial Padding-only Traffic Analysis Defense (PETS 2024)
properties.technique: Competing neural networks generate dummy traffic to defeat analysis
properties.result: Reduces attacker accuracy by 61.5% with moderate overhead
properties.relevance: Padding-based defense applicable to session-router traffic analysis

properties.title: libsodium crypto_box_seal — Nonce Derivation Concern
properties.concern: Nonce derived from ephemeral_pk + recipient_pk — ephemeral key reuse breaks confidentiality
properties.mitigation: Secret key overwritten after function returns — prevents accidental reuse
properties.overall_assessment: No major vulnerabilities found in libsodium security review
properties.relevance: Our session init uses crypto_box_seal — ensure ephemeral key never reused

properties.title: Session: End-To-End Encrypted Conversations With Minimal Metadata Leakage
properties.relevance: Original Session protocol design paper — describes threat model and security guarantees

properties.title: Thirteen Years of Tor Attacks (GitHub catalog)
properties.relevance: Comprehensive catalog of attack techniques — many applicable to Session's 3-hop routing

properties.name: Probe Categories
properties.description: Security probe categories derived from research

properties.name: Wire Format Fuzzing
properties.rationale: BT encoding mismatches caused all 30+ critical bugs in our rewrite — same class of bugs likely exists in upstream parser
probes: Malformed BT dict — missing closing 'e'
BT dict with duplicate keys
BT dict with keys out of lexicographic order
Session init with truncated sealed box
Session init with oversized sealed box (>MAX)
Session init with wrong handshake type byte
Session accept before session init
Path build frame not exactly 169 bytes
Path build with 0 real hops
Path build with >8 hops (overflow BUILD_LENGTH)
Inner payload BT dict with extra unknown keys
Inner payload with negative lifetime
Session data with tampered session tag
Session data with tampered pivot ID
Control message with empty method name
Control message with 1MB body

properties.name: Cryptographic Boundary Testing
properties.rationale: Key derivation had 6 critical mismatches — boundary conditions in crypto are where silent failures hide
probes: Session key derivation with all-zero DH result (low-order point)
Session key derivation with identity element as X25519 pubkey
ML-KEM encapsulation with corrupted ciphertext (single bit flip)
ML-KEM with wrong-size ciphertext (1087 or 1089 bytes)
Sealed box with recipient's own pubkey as sender
Sealed box decryption with wrong key (must fail, not crash)
AEAD decryption with tampered ciphertext (each byte position)
AEAD decryption with tampered 4-byte tag
AEAD with maximum-length plaintext
Nonce counter overflow (2^64 messages on one session)
Session tag collision — two sessions with same tag value
Ed25519 signature with all-zero signature bytes
Ed25519 verify with small-order public key

properties.name: Protocol State Machine
properties.rationale: Quarkslab found state-related issues in Session app — same class applies to router
probes: Session init without prior path build
Double session init (replay)
Session accept with wrong session tag
Session data before handshake completes
Session data after session close
Path build with expired lifetime (0 seconds)
Path build with far-future lifetime (MAX_UINT32)
Control message with unknown method name
Path switch to non-existent path
Concurrent session init from both sides (race)
Session close then immediate re-init (rapid cycling)

properties.name: QUIC Transport Layer
properties.rationale: QUIC-Fuzz found 10 vulns in major implementations; QUIC-LEAK shows pre-handshake DoS; oxen-libquic had crash bugs
probes: Connection with wrong ALPN string
Connection with empty ALPN
Rapid connection open/close cycling (100+ connections)
Maximum concurrent connections to single endpoint
Datagram larger than QUIC max datagram frame
Datagram with zero bytes
BTStream with command name >64KB
BTStream with malformed BT-encoded command body
Connection with invalid TLS certificate
Connection from non-Ed25519 key (wrong key type)
QUIC-loris: open connection, send 1 byte/second
Pre-handshake flood (QUIC-LEAK pattern)
Connection migration mid-session

properties.name: 0-RTT Replay Attacks
properties.rationale: Our rewrite enables 0-RTT with 1-minute anti-replay — need to verify the window actually works
probes: 0-RTT replay within anti-replay window (should reject)
0-RTT replay after anti-replay window expires
0-RTT with expired session ticket (>24 hours)
0-RTT data that triggers state mutation (idempotency test)
Multiple 0-RTT attempts with same ticket simultaneously

properties.name: Bootstrap & Identity
properties.rationale: Quarkslab's severe finding was TLS verification on node list — bootstrap is the trust root
probes: bootstrap.signed with invalid Ed25519 signature
bootstrap.signed with signature over modified payload
RC with expired timestamp (>30 days old)
RC with future timestamp (clock skew attack)
RC with timestamp = 0
RC with non-routable IPv4 (10.x, 192.168.x)
RC with non-routable IPv6 (fe80::, ::1)
RC exceeding 2048 byte max size
RC with unknown version number
RC with missing required fields
Bootstrap fetch response with oversized zstd payload (>20MB)
Bootstrap fetch response with zstd bomb (small compressed, huge decompressed)
Bootstrap file with 10,000 RCs (resource exhaustion)
Bootstrap file with duplicate router IDs

properties.name: Resource Exhaustion
properties.rationale: QUIC-LEAK proved pre-handshake memory exhaustion is exploitable; oxen-libquic had crash-on-unexpected-input
probes: Memory: accumulate path builds without completing sessions
Memory: open sessions without sending data (idle accumulation)
CPU: flood with computationally expensive sealed box operations
CPU: rapid session init/accept cycling (key derivation spam)
File descriptors: exhaust via QUIC connection flood
Disk: trigger excessive logging via malformed messages
NodeDB: insert 100,000 RCs (routing table bloat)
Path build flood: 1000 concurrent path builds

properties.name: Traffic Analysis & Deanonymization
properties.rationale: 32% of Tor research is deanon attacks; Session's 3-hop routing faces identical threat class. Sybil cost is the main defense.
probes: Timing correlation: measure latency variance across paths
Traffic fingerprinting: identify message types by size patterns
Path selection bias: verify path selection is uniformly random
Sybil detection: how many nodes needed to control a path
Padding analysis: do different message types have distinguishable sizes
Session linkability: can repeated sessions to same destination be linked
Guard node detection: is first hop reused across sessions
properties.note: These are analysis probes, not attacks — measuring resistance, not exploiting

properties.title: No security audit exists for session-router itself
properties.detail: Quarkslab audited the Session app (Android/iOS/Desktop) but NOT the session-router/lokinet routing layer. The transport, path building, session negotiation, and exit mode have never been independently audited.

properties.title: Protocol V2 will change key exchange — our implementation needs updating
properties.detail: Session Protocol V2 introduces rotating keys, per-device ephemeral keys, and ML-KEM changes. Our current session init/accept implements V1 wire format. V2 specs expected 2026.

properties.title: oxen-libquic has history of crash-on-unexpected-input
properties.detail: iOS QUIC connections uncovered crash cases that affected storage servers AND other onion path users. A crash anywhere on the onion path cascades to all connections through that node. Mandatory service node upgrades were required to fix.

properties.title: Session V1 protocol deliberately lacks PFS
properties.detail: Session removed Perfect Forward Secrecy from V1 protocol, arguing 'physical access is total access'. V2 will re-add it. Until V2 ships, long-term key compromise exposes all historical messages.

properties.title: Pre-handshake resource exhaustion is a proven QUIC attack vector
properties.detail: CVE-2025-54939 (QUIC-LEAK) demonstrated memory exhaustion before handshake in LSQUIC, bypassing all standard QUIC protections. Same attack pattern should be tested against oxen-libquic.

properties.title: BT encoding parsers have no published fuzz testing
properties.detail: No bencode/BT-encoding fuzzing research exists in public literature. Session-router's BT parser (oxen-encoding) processes every message on the wire. An exploitable parser bug = remote code execution on every service node.

properties.description: Security gaps identified from web research

properties.name: Security Probe Tooling
properties.description: Tools, frameworks, and techniques for building the probe system

properties.name: AFL++
properties.key_feature: Persistent mode — 2-20x speed increase, SUT stays alive between iterations
properties.relevance: Primary fuzzing engine for wire format and BT parser fuzzing
properties.integration: Compatible with libFuzzer harnesses — change compiler from clang++ to afl-clang-fast++
properties.stateful_support: AFL_LOOP macro keeps forkserver alive; AFLNet extension adds state-aware network protocol fuzzing
properties.recommendation: Use persistent mode with custom BT-encoding-aware mutator for maximum coverage of session-router wire formats

properties.name: libFuzzer
properties.key_feature: LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput() is the defacto standard harness interface
properties.relevance: Write harnesses once, run with both libFuzzer and AFL++
properties.integration: Built into Clang, no external dependencies. Compatible with sanitizers.
properties.recommendation: Write all fuzzing harnesses as LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput — this is the universal interface that works with libFuzzer, AFL++, honggfuzz, and OSS-Fuzz

properties.name: LibAFLstar
properties.key_feature: State-aware queues, state scheduler, partial message sequences, persistent mode
properties.results: 30x faster than AFLNet/ChatAFL, 1.4x more coverage on FTP/RTSP/HTTP
properties.relevance: Purpose-built for stateful protocol fuzzing — session-router is a stateful protocol
properties.technique: Takes seed traces + state model as input, generates partial message sequence prefixes to reach specific states before fuzzing
properties.recommendation: Best candidate for protocol state machine probes — model session-router states (idle→path_built→session_init→session_active→session_closed) and fuzz transitions

properties.name: Fuzi_Q
properties.key_feature: Intercepts QUIC messages BEFORE encryption — fuzzes plaintext, not ciphertext
properties.technique: Determines encryption point per connection (initial processed, handshake confirmed, closing), progresses to that state, then fuzzes
properties.limitation: Tied to Picoquic stack, not oxen-libquic — needs adaptation
properties.relevance: Solves the critical problem: fuzzing encrypted QUIC mostly tests crypto code, not protocol logic. Same approach needed for oxen-libquic.
properties.recommendation: Study Fuzi_Q's pre-encryption interception pattern and replicate it for oxen-libquic. Don't use Fuzi_Q directly — adapt the technique.

properties.name: Boofuzz
properties.key_feature: Define protocol states (handshake→auth→data), fuzz each state independently. Built-in web UI on port 26000.
properties.relevance: Quick prototyping of probe sequences before building C++ harnesses. Good for black-box testing of upstream binaries.
properties.recommendation: Use Boofuzz for initial black-box probing of upstream session-router binary. Graduate to AFL++/LibAFLstar for coverage-guided fuzzing of our rewrite.

properties.name: Cryptofuzz
properties.key_feature: Differential fuzzing across dozens of crypto libraries. Runs on OSS-Fuzz continuously.
properties.bugs_found: ~35 bugs in stable releases of major crypto libraries, including CVE-2022-2097 in OpenSSL AES-OCB
properties.approach: Same input to multiple implementations, compare outputs. Mutation-driven with code coverage guidance.
properties.libsodium_status: libsodium support planned/partial — EverCrypt fork fuzzes against libsodium and BoringSSL
properties.relevance: Our rewrite and upstream both use libsodium — differential fuzz our crypto layer against upstream's to find implementation divergence
properties.recommendation: Build a differential harness: feed same crypto inputs to both our session_keys/aead/sealed_box and upstream's equivalents. Any output divergence = interop bug or security bug.

properties.name: RapidCheck
properties.key_feature: QuickCheck for C++ — state facts about code, framework generates random data to falsify. Auto-shrinks to minimal counterexample.
properties.relevance: Test cryptographic properties: decrypt(encrypt(m))=m, verify(sign(m, sk), pk)=true, key_derivation is deterministic
properties.recommendation: Use RapidCheck for crypto property tests: round-trip encryption, signature verification, key derivation consistency. Catches edge cases that unit tests miss. Integrates with Catch2.

properties.name: Clang Sanitizers (ASan, MSan, UBSan, TSan)

sanitizers.ASan: Address Sanitizer — buffer overflows, use-after-free, double-free. Shadow memory based.
sanitizers.MSan: Memory Sanitizer — reads from uninitialized memory. Critical for crypto code where uninitialized bytes = key leakage.
sanitizers.UBSan: Undefined Behavior Sanitizer — integer overflow, null deref, alignment. Crypto code is full of integer math.
sanitizers.TSan: Thread Sanitizer — data races. Our rewrite uses event loop but upstream uses NullMutex.

properties.constraint: ASan and MSan are mutually exclusive (conflicting shadow memory). Run separate fuzzing campaigns for each.
properties.oss_fuzz_stats: OSS-Fuzz found 13,000+ vulnerabilities and 50,000+ bugs across 1,000 projects using sanitizers + fuzzing
properties.recommendation: Every fuzzing harness MUST be compiled with sanitizers. Run three campaigns: (1) AFL++ + ASan + UBSan, (2) AFL++ + MSan, (3) AFL++ + TSan. This catches memory bugs, uninitialized reads, undefined behavior, and races.

properties.name: OSS-Fuzz / ClusterFuzzLite
properties.key_feature: Free continuous fuzzing for open source. Runs libFuzzer + AFL++ + honggfuzz with all sanitizers.
properties.integration: Requires Dockerfile, build.sh, project.yaml. Qualification: project must serve critical purpose.
properties.clusterfuzzlite: Lightweight version for CI/CD — runs on GitHub Actions, no Google infrastructure needed
properties.relevance: Our rewrite is GPL-3.0 open source — qualifies for OSS-Fuzz. Continuous fuzzing catches regressions.
properties.recommendation: Phase 1: ClusterFuzzLite in GitHub Actions for our repo (immediate). Phase 2: Apply to OSS-Fuzz for continuous infrastructure (after probe framework stabilizes).

properties.name: libprotobuf-mutator (LPM)
properties.key_feature: Describe input format as protobuf message, LPM generates structured mutations. Integrates with libFuzzer.
properties.technique: Define .proto for BT-encoded dicts, LPM mutates fields while preserving structure. Catches bugs in parser edge cases, not just random bytes.
properties.bitcoin_usage: Bitcoin Core uses LPM for protocol fuzzing (PR #26975)
properties.relevance: BT encoding has a fixed structure (dicts with typed fields). LPM can mutate within that structure to find parser bugs that random fuzzing misses.
properties.recommendation: Define session_init.proto, session_accept.proto, path_build.proto, relay_contact.proto. LPM generates valid-ish BT messages with mutated fields — more effective than random bytes for finding parser bugs.

properties.name: ProVerif / Tamarin
properties.key_feature: Symbolic analysis of cryptographic protocols — proves security properties or finds attacks
properties.technique: Model protocol as process calculus, verify secrecy/authentication/forward-secrecy properties
properties.recent_work: 2025 ACM CCS paper: formal verification of crypto protocol implementations in Rust using ProVerif + SSProve + F*
properties.limitation: Models protocol logic, not implementation bugs. Complementary to fuzzing.
properties.relevance: Can formally verify that session-router's key exchange achieves expected security properties (secrecy, authentication, PFS when V2 ships)
properties.recommendation: Phase 7 stretch goal — model session key derivation and session handshake in ProVerif. Proves protocol-level correctness that no amount of fuzzing can guarantee.

properties.name: Differential Testing
properties.description: Same input to multiple implementations, compare outputs. Discrepancy = bug in at least one.
properties.key_insight: We have TWO implementations of the same protocol — upstream and rewrite. This is the ideal setup for differential testing.
properties.bugs_found_elsewhere: Cryptofuzz: ~35 bugs in crypto libraries. Frankencerts: 208 discrepancies in SSL/TLS implementations.
properties.application: Feed identical wire messages to both upstream and rewrite. Any behavioral difference (accept vs reject, different output, crash vs clean error) reveals a bug.
properties.recommendation: This is our highest-value technique. We have two implementations — use them against each other. Build a differential harness that replays the same BT-encoded messages through both parsers.

properties.name: Stateful Protocol Fuzzing
properties.description: Fuzz multi-message sequences, not single messages. Must reach correct protocol state before triggering bugs.
properties.key_insight: A malicious message must be sent from the right state — fuzzer must provide multiple messages to reach the correct state first
properties.state_model: session-router states: idle → path_building → path_built → session_init_sent → session_active → session_closing → closed
properties.recommendation: Model session-router's state machine explicitly. Use LibAFLstar's state scheduler to fuzz transitions. Priority: fuzz the session_init→session_active transition (key derivation + sealed box + BT encoding all in one path).

properties.name: Structure-Aware Fuzzing
properties.description: Mutate within known input structure rather than random bytes. Reaches deeper code paths.
properties.key_insight: Random bytes rarely produce valid BT-encoded dicts. Structure-aware mutators generate valid-ish inputs that pass initial parsing and reach deeper logic.
properties.application: BT encoding is structured: dicts have string keys in lexicographic order, typed values, specific field names. A custom mutator that understands BT structure will find bugs that random fuzzing never reaches.
properties.recommendation: Write a BT-encoding-aware custom mutator (LLVMFuzzerCustomMutator) that generates syntactically valid BT dicts with fuzzed field values. This is more effective than LPM for bencode because bencode is simpler than protobuf.

properties.title: X41 Security Audit of ngtcp2 + nghttp3 (2025)
properties.result: Zero vulnerabilities found. 3 informational findings in ngtcp2 (no security impact).
findings: Stateless reset token checked against retired connections (RFC 9000 violation, informational)
Timing side channel leaks packet number length (informational, low impact)
properties.relevance: ngtcp2 is the recommended QUIC backend and was found clean. oxen-libquic is a separate implementation — never audited. The contrast highlights our gap.
properties.recommendation: Reference this audit as the gold standard. Our probe system should test everything X41 tested, plus session-router-specific protocol logic.

properties.title: Zen-AI-Pentest: AI-Powered Penetration Testing (2026)
properties.technique: Autonomous agents + Nmap + Metasploit for recon, scanning, exploitation, reporting
properties.relevance: AI-guided probe sequencing could automate probe category prioritization based on intermediate findings
properties.recommendation: Interesting but premature for our use case. Manual probe design with AFL++/LibAFLstar is higher value than AI-guided exploration for a protocol we already understand deeply.
